title: Backpressure spillover and dequeue strategy for GPU capacity events
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity event on 2026-03-08 we observed sustained GPU pool saturation that manifested as a steadily increasing request queue (>10k pending) and large numbers of early request timeouts and throttles. This ticket captures the incident follow-up work: implement defensive backpressure at the edge, introduce a controlled spillover path to warm standby capacity, and improve dequeue behavior to prioritize low-cost short requests so overall successful throughput improves while we scale.
timeline: 2026-03-08 01:22 UTC: Alert - hosted-gpu-pool-1 queue length crossed 2k
2026-03-08 01:26 UTC: Autoscaler attempted scale but <30% of new nodes became ready due to provisioning lag and container cold-start; queue continued growing
2026-03-08 01:40 UTC: Admission controller fell back to simple token-bucket which allowed large bursts to enqueue; observed KV cache pressure and degraded per-token throughput
2026-03-08 02:05 UTC: We enabled emergency shedding for non-P0 customers and reduced queue by ~40% but tail latencies remained high

Post-incident: spike traced to a combination of an admission-control regression (recent change reverted batching preference) and a placement heuristic that prevented immediate reuse of pre-warmed slots
root_cause: Admission control regression: a 2026-02 change to the edge admission controller inadvertently disabled short-request prioritization; large generation requests could enqueue ahead of small helper calls
Autoscaler visibility gap: the autoscaler decision only used CPU/GPU utilization signals and did not consider pending queue growth rate (requests/sec queued), so scale triggers were delayed
Placement/pre-warm mismatch: pre-warmed spare nodes existed but placement policy required a stricter model-compatibility check that caused additional cold-starts instead of reusing warm capacity
KV cache churn: sudden influx of heterogeneous requests caused KV cache churn and reduced per-token throughput on saturated GPUs
action_items: (A1) Revert/patch admission-controller regression to restore short-request prioritization and implement deterministic dequeue priority for requests <500ms estimated compute - owner: Miguel - due 2026-03-15
(A2) Add queue-growth-rate metric to autoscaler inputs and implement a fast-path scale-up when queue growth > 500 req/min for 3 consecutive minutes - owner: Infra Autoscale Team - due 2026-03-18

(A3) Implement spillover lane: a controlled path that sends lowest-priority requests to pre-warmed 'spill' GPU pool with best-effort SLAs to keep main pool focused - owner: Serving Runtime - due 2026-03-22
(A4) Add admission-tokens at edge with explicit per-customer budgets + quick reject path to avoid long tail queueing for misbehaving clients - owner: API Edge - due 2026-03-20
(A5) Improve cache warm/reuse policy to allow placement to reuse pre-warmed nodes for compatible quantized model variants - owner: Runtime Ops - due 2026-03-25
(A6) Post-deploy validation: run 10 synthetic surge scenarios (varied sequence lengths and request mixes) and verify queue growth and 95th percentile latency goals - owner: SRE - due 2026-03-28
(A7) Create runbook update for GPU exhaustion events: include triage checklist, quick-shed commands, and rollback steps - owner: SRE - due 2026-03-14
decisions: Implement multi-stage backpressure: edge token-bucket + local admission + prioritized dequeue within serving nodes
Spillover will be best-effort and billed differently; will not be used for enterprise SLA customers unless explicitly configured
Autoscaler will be modified to consume an 'effective queue' signal (combination of pending requests and average per-request token cost)
Short requests (<500ms estimate) will be favored in dequeue ordering to improve successful request rate during constrained windows

acceptance_criteria: Prod-like load tests: when synthetic 2x surge applied, max queue length < 2k and 95p latency for priority requests improves by at least 30% compared to baseline
Autoscaler triggers within 3 minutes of sustained queue growth > 500 req/min and new nodes reduce pending queue by >= 40% within 7 minutes
Spillover lane operational with documented billing and explicit opt-in configuration; non-enterprise customers see best-effort behavior
Runbook updated and SRE on-call trained on new quick-shed commands
